prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Create ONE new independent frame 01 of the SAME boy's NORTH-running cycle. Primary reference1 locks head, full-canvas camera, short-body scale and identity; reference2 shows opposite support anatomy, not a scale change. Remaining references are committed NORTH identity, front costume identity only, and approved painted style.
Strict NORTH BACK VIEW, NO face or eye. Anatomical RIGHT always screen-right holding gold thunder wand; LEFT always screen-left holding rectangular gold talisman. Preserve layered round brown hair, ponytail gold ribbon/turquoise beads, ivory/gold/navy short robe with central gold back lightning, navy trousers, white crossed calf wraps, black/gold boots. Same head width/height and camera as image1; do not enlarge or stretch the character.
EXACT NEW PHASE: RIGHT leg (screen-right) stays planted in load acceptance. Its knee bends a little more than frame00; pelvis lowers a small amount. LEFT recovery heel begins to descend forward beneath the coat but remains airborne. Right wand arm eases from back toward middle, left talisman arm from forward toward middle. One loaded foot, no high hop.
Keep all knee-shin-ankle axes pointed north along travel, natural compact running lanes, no outward duck feet or combat horse stance. Clearly show both short calves/boots despite robe, anatomical joints continuous, no duplicated hands/feet. Head and pelvis may only bob slightly for this phase while camera stays fixed. Ground/root same as image1, about x=.50 y=.92; respect perspective rather than forcing both boots to one line. Full figure, boots inside canvas. Same polished painted materials and finish. Transparent RGBA, native square single frame >=1024, no drawn ground/shadow/effects/text/grid, no mirror/copy of another frame.
